Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the short version below and attached a concise SLO definition doc that matches what we publish to customers (SLO_Metrics_Definition_v1.pdf). Happy to expand any section.

How we measure availability and latency (high level):
- Measurement points: edge ingress + service-layer responder. We compute per-request latency at the service layer and mark success/failure at the final delivery path.
- Sampling & aggregation: all requests are recorded as telemetry. For customer-facing SLOs we apply an aggregation window of 1 minute for rolling p95/p99 and a 5-minute window for short-term availability buckets.
- Definitions:
  - "Available": percentage of 1-minute buckets where error rate < 1% for that customer route; availability is reported as a rolling 30-day percentage for contract purposes.
  - "Latency p95/p99": computed across successful requests within each 1-minute bucket and then aggregated to hourly rollups for trend dashboards.
- Alerting: alert rules operate on aggregated buckets (1-minute and 5-minute) with depletion thresholds. We also support anomaly detectors that look at raw event streams for incidents that aggregation might mask.

On dashboard access and exception windows: short answer — yes, we can provide a read-only dashboard link scoped to your account, plus an option for a time-limited elevated view for verification. Typical controls we apply:
- Access type: read-only Grafana link + pre-filtered queries for your account ID. No raw logs by default.
- Exception mode: for procurement verification we can open a 30-day "evidence window" where support engineers can enable a temporary view of higher-granularity telemetry (event-level traces) under an NDA and with strict RBAC (audit logs enabled).
- Retention: dashboard rollups are visible per the contract (default 90 days for fine-grained metrics; 13 months for 1-hour rollups). Event-level retention is shorter (14 days) and can be extended under custom contracts.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will share the SLO doc (attached) and a sample dashboard screenshot (attached).
2) If that looks good, we can provision a read-only link for you to review.
3) If procurement requires, we’ll open an evidence window and route the request through Security/SaaS ops (Ben is cc'd for the RBAC/approval flow).

Adding a couple of operational notes on sampling and alerts that procurement tends to ask about:
- Sampling bias: we do not downsample for SLO calculation; every request is included in the 1-minute buckets. Where customers have extremely high QPS, we use lossless aggregation at proxy level and then compute percentiles from histograms to avoid OOMs.
- Maintenance windows: scheduled maintenance that falls into a customer-notified window is excluded from availability calculations (we store maintenance annotations on the 1-minute buckets).
- Alert cadence: production alerts are tiered: P0 (immediate paging) when 5-minute availability drops below contractual threshold; P1 (email/Slack) for sustained deviations in hour rollups.
- Canary verification: we recommend a short canary run (48–72 hours) of your representative load against your dedicated route before final sign-off. We can coordinate that if you want.

On the evidence window: we control event-level access through session-limited tokens and require an approved justification form (we typically ask procurement to sign the evidence access addendum). Ben — can you confirm the RBAC checklist we will require for Stratus?

-Marissa

Hey Samir — quick answers and the operational path forward: 

1) p99 fidelity: the dashboard p99 uses histogram-derived percentiles which are equivalent to raw-computed percentiles for the same sample set within our aggregation windows. If you replay a subset, small quantization differences can appear due to histogram bucketing, but they are within typical decimal variance (<2–3%). We can produce a side-by-side runbook to show the computation if you want exact parity testing.

2) 7-day subset: yes. We can expose event-level traces for a specified 7-day window and accept a list of up to 50 request-ids for targeted lookups. This will be enabled only for the evidence window and requires an approved justification form plus an executed data access addendum.

3) Audit evidence: all access is logged. The logs include user identity, IP, time, and query scope. We will provide an export of the audit records covering the evidence window on request (CSV).

Operational steps (to avoid delay):
- I will provision a read-only Grafana link scoped to Stratus that should be live within 24 hours after you confirm the account ID. Link will enforce IP restrictions if requested.
- If you want the 7-day event-level view, confirm the 7-day dates and the list of up to 50 request-ids; we will route the request to Security and enable a session-limited view for a maximum of 14 days (shorter than the full 30-day procurement window).
- Ben + Jonas will be the approvers on RBAC and any billing/contract changes.

I attached the SLO doc and a screenshot of the dashboard (SLO_Metrics_Definition_v1.pdf; redwood-dashboard-sample.png). Please reply with the account ID and whether you want the event-level subset.
